title: Wholemeal Irish Brown Soda Bread with Oats
summary: Wholemeal and plain flour, oats, bicarbonate, salt and a little brown sugar are stirred with buttermilk and melted butter, shaped into a round, cut with a deep cross and baked to 93 °C.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the flours, oats, bicarbonate, salt and sugar together. Add the melted butter and buttermilk and stir quickly into a soft, sticky dough. Do not knead.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Tip onto a floured surface and shape gently into a round about 18 cm across. Put on the tray, scatter with oats and cut a deep cross across the top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake straight away for 40-45 minutes until browned, hollow-sounding underneath and 93 °C in the centre.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Wrap in a tea towel for a soft crust, or leave uncovered for a crisp one, and cool at least 30 minutes before slicing.

tips: Work quickly: the bicarbonate starts reacting as soon as it meets the buttermilk.
A wet dough makes a lighter loaf, so do not add too much flour.
The deep cross lets heat reach the centre so it bakes through evenly.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature and eat within 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Refresh in a hot oven for a few minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
